prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Race condition in post_writer: the task group spawns post_writer with start_soon and the caller proceeds (yields/starts writing) before post_writer has actually entered its loop and is ready to receive messages, which can drop the first message(s) sent on write_stream and hang the client. members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in post_writer: the task group spawns post_writer with start_soon and the caller proceeds (yields/starts writing) before post_writer has actually entered its loop and is ready to receive messages, which can drop the first message(s) sent on write_stream and hang the client. Both PRs fix it identically by adding a task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED parameter to post_writer and calling task_status.started(None) once the stream context is entered, so the caller can tg.start() and block until post_writer is actually ready.

clusters.pick_reason: #2215's diff is against a stale version of stdio.py (still using anyio.create_memory_object_stream(0) directly), while #2654 and #2552 are both against the current file after it was refactored to create_context_streams(...) — #2215 would need to be rebased and re-resolved against that refactor. #2654 also fixes the blocking behavior by default (buffer=1) without requiring any caller opt-in, whereas #2215 only exposes a configurable parameter that defaults to the same buffer=0 that causes the blocking, so it doesn't resolve the underlying issue unless a caller explicitly changes it. #2654 additionally ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the stall scenario directly.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both touch the exact same line — the buffer size passed when constructing the stdio write_stream (memory object stream) — to address stdout backpressure/blocking in the stdio transport. #2215 makes the size a caller-supplied parameter (default 0, i.e. no behavior change unless a caller opts in). #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1 so the fix applies out-of-the-box, specifically to let a handler queue its final response while an earlier progress notification is still being flushed to stdout.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2555 fixes the root cause with an idiomatic per-class __reduce__ override on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, reconstructing directly from the subclass's own typed fields (_elicitations, message) rather than round-tripping through ErrorData. Its diff also includes test coverage in tests/shared/test_exceptions.py. PR #2478 instead patches this by hardcoding a subclass type-check (if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError) inside a new base-level _restore_mcp_error dispatcher, which is more fragile (base class must know about specific subclasses and needs updating for any future MCPError subclass with a non-standard constructor), and its shown diff includes no corresponding test changes.
